notes: v243 — three owner-named fixes from his Fri Oct 23, 2026 evening screen recordings on live v242. (1) CONNECT-SENDDOC GENERAL SHARE PICKER (21:15 + scope correction 21:18 MDT: 'this shouldn't be damage photo, but generally any image from the directory or document from the directory or messages... Or really anything'): the Send-doc door now reaches the app's actual stores — damage reports, haul-ticket photos (dispatch records), fuel receipt photos, PTI defect photos, session odometer photos, the truck's sticker photos (active truck's chain), issued invoices, manifest entries, locations. Root causes fixed together: the damage package never carried the photo itself ({title, desc, date} only, read from fields the module never writes); the other stores had no kind at all; and dmg_reports was missing from the sync layer's record-union list, so a stale-stamped cloud copy could wipe the phone's saved damage reports at pull — the exact v241 fuel-loss class (now unioned by tab+desc+at+dispatch identity, photo-bearing copy wins). The picker is profile-aware via the v242 seam (the ACTIVE profile's records; unstamped = Profile 1) and stays bound by the v242 Connect fence: a Profile-1 item dated on a day carrying another profile's stamp is not offered, and while a non-main profile is active nothing queues (a plain line says why). An empty kind is a door, not a wall: one tap straight into the owning module's create flow. Damage reports are now born with a real date + their profile stamp. Named honestly: the app holds no separate shareable 'messages' store — its stored texts are the manifest feed (covered) and the AI chat history (his private conversation, not a shareable) — and inbound Connect shares (nav_shares / landed items) are received items, not his to re-send. (2) PROFILE1-LABEL-WRONG (21:24 MDT): Preferences + the dashboard chip labelled his real Profile 1 'Tester · Truck 07'. The label derives from the persisted work_profiles record (seeded from onboarding.contractingCo), and unlike the v216-gated onboarding slot or the v219-namespaced Connect keys, that key carried no account owner — a state seeded under another account's working copy on the same phone became his Profile 1. The seam now stamps the state with its account owner at every persist, treats a different account's state as absent (derives fresh from his own onboarding), and heals a lone Profile 1 whose company disagrees with his own contracting company (the working copy IS that profile). The exact field the wrong label derived from: work_profiles.list[0].company, seeded by derive-on-read from onboarding.contractingCo. (3) OWN-WAGE-AS-CONNECTED-DRIVER (21:24 MDT): Preferences' 'Drivers' wages' card listed 'Connected driver $29.00/hour' — his own wage returning via a self-pair: CP.fetchRecords enumerated his own records doc as a peer's, P&L cached its driverWage into __peer_wages with no self-exclusion, and the card listed every cached uid. Fixed at both doors: P&L's crew fetch never caches the account's own uid, and the Preferences card filters its own uid out on read (a pre-fix cache renders clean too); with no other drivers the card shows none — not himself.
